rows.reasoning: For 7 selections from 3 types with repetition, stars and bars gives C(7+3−1,7)=C(9,7)=36.
Five distinct people around a circle modulo rotation: (5-1)!=24.
The first digit has 4 nonzero choices; each of the remaining three digits has 5 choices, giving 4·5^3=500.
The one-or-two-step recurrence gives F_9=34 ways to climb 8 steps.
The sum is 2^n; 1000<2^n<10000 gives n=10,11,12,13, so max-min=3.
The shaded entries are the C(n,1) and C(n,2) diagonals for n=1..10, whose sums are C(11,2)=55 and C(11,3)=165; total 220.
Fix the conductor to remove rotation; the two violinists occupy the two adjacent seats in 2! ways, and the other three performers in 3! ways.
There are five regions including the center disk. Choose 5 of 7 colors and biject them to the five regions, then quotient by the four rotations: C(7,5)·5!/4=630.

There are three table corners with two adjacent seats associated to each. Assign the two labeled men to distinct corners and choose one of two seats at each (3·2·2·2=24); arrange four women in 4! ways and divide by 3 rotations: 192.

All arrangements of the multiset are 7!/(2!2!); the relative order of 4,5,6 is fixed in one of 3! orders, giving 1260/6=210.
To obtain x^10 choose k=2 factors of 2x^3; coefficient C(6,2)·2^2·(-3)^4=4860.

Descending lexicographic order: 64 numbers start with 7; among those starting with 5, 16 have second digit 7, 4 have prefix 55 and third digit 7, and 1 has prefix 555 and last digit 7. Thus 5555 is 86th.
Onto functions from a 5-element set to a 3-element set: 3^5−3·2^5+3=150.
Set x'=x−1,y'=y−1,z'=z−1; then nonnegative sum ≤7, equivalent by slack variable to C(10,3)=120.
Modulo (x²+3)², put t=x²+3; (t+1)^5≡1+5t. At x=1 this is 1+5·4=21.
Write the four function values as 2^{e_i}, e_i∈{1,2,3}; their product condition requires sum e_i=9. Equivalently deficits 3−e_i sum to 3 with each at most 2: C(6,3)−4=16.

There are C(6,2)C(10,2)=675 distributions before the each-box-total≥2 restriction. For a fixed box with total 0 or 1, counts are 45+36+40=121; for a fixed pair both totals≤1 there are 9 configurations. Inclusion-exclusion gives 675−3·121+3·9=339.

Positive solutions to sum 14 are C(13,3)=286. Excluding any coordinate ≥9 removes 10 per coordinate, leaving 246 under the upper bound 8. All-odd solutions correspond to four 0..3 values summing 5: C(8,3)−4C(4,3)=40. Therefore at least one even is 246−40=206.

Elements 5,6,7 belong to A∩B and not C. Each of 8,9,10 has four allowed memberships: A only, B only, both, or C only. Exclude C empty (3^3=27 patterns) and then exclude A=B with C nonempty (2^3−1=7): 64−27−7=30.

Let a=f(1), b=f(3), c=f(5), with a≤b≤c and f(c)=3. For c=2 there are 6 triples and f(2) is fixed, giving 6·5=30; for c=3, b=3 and there are 3 triples, with f(2),f(4) free, giving 75; for c=4, f(4)=3, there are 15 triples and f(2) is free, giving 75. c=1,5 impossible. Total 180.
After including 2 and 3, the other 25 elements must form an odd-cardinality subset. Half of all subsets have odd size, so the count is 2^24 and a=24.
